title: Sonic was originally a rabbit.
description:
Sonic was originally a rabbit. Sega's 1990 internal contest to find a new mascot drew around 200 submitted designs.

Roughly how many characters Sega's own staff submitted before anyone had heard of Sonic.

It picked up objects with its ears and threw them at enemies, and that slowed everything down. Programmer Yuji Naka said plainly that game speed could not be maintained with that action.

So the choice narrowed to two animals that roll into a ball: an armadillo, or a hedgehog. The hedgehog won because its quills looked like an attack. The armadillo's shell just looked like armour.

The winning design was not even new. It was an old doodle Ohshima had already thrown away.

Sources:
- https://www.vice.com/en/article/sonic-the-hedgehog-was-almost-sonic-the-rabbit/: an excerpt from Sega's own Sonic the Hedgehog 25th Anniversary Art Book, establishing that Sega's 1990 internal mascot contest drew around 200 character designs from staff across Sega Japan and Sega of America, that artist Naoto Ohshima's winning design was originally a rabbit with a bow tie and long ears that picked up and threw objects, that programmer Yuji Naka is quoted saying game speed could not be maintained with that action, that the team then narrowed the choice to an armadillo or a hedgehog and picked the hedgehog because its quills read better as an attack than the armadillo's leathery shell, and that the final design reused an old discarded doodle of Ohshima's called Mr Needlemouse.
- https://www.techradar.com/news/sonic-boom-sega-designer-tells-the-origin-story-of-a-gaming-legend: a 2021 interview with designer Hirokazu Yasuhara confirming the internal contest was launched to replace Sega's previous mascot Alex Kidd, that Ohshima submitted a range of designs including an armadillo, a porcupine, a dog, a rabbit and a moustached man who became Doctor Robotnik, and giving the game's release date of 23 June 1991.
